headline: High: MemMachine’s MCP/networked defaults create prompt-injection and data-leakage risk when paired with a content-writing agent, while the repo-only agent adds no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python interfaces, so it can ingest external content and context by default; a content-writing agent can supply untrusted text that may be treated as instructions. The Awesome-Prompt-Engineering repo is non-runnable and provides no isolation or provenance controls, so the pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF MemMachine consumes content from the content-writing agent via MCP or REST without provenance tagging, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected through copy-paste or shared prompts, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted text.
Add a provenance prefix to all cross-agent messages.
Require a human review step before executing instructions extracted from agent A.
Use a read-only handoff format for shared content.
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation on all MCP payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and has allowlisted network egress, so any shared workspace or forwarded content can leak sensitive context outward. Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is a docs-only repository, so it is not itself a data sink, but it can still be used as a bridge for copying sensitive prompts into MemMachine.
conditions: IF user prompts or conversation snippets are copied from the repo into MemMachine, those data classes can be exposed to its backend.
IF MemMachine forwards context over network egress, sensitive preferences may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive text in shared prompts.
Turn off network egress for test runs if possible.
Use a separate workspace for the repo and MemMachine.
Redact personal facts before handoff.
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on outbound context.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The pair shows no overlapping write or mutable-resource permissions: Awesome-Prompt-Engineering is non-runnable and has no write surfaces, while MemMachine exposes APIs but no filesystem or git write capability is documented. A conflict pathway exists only if an external orchestrator grants both write access, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same mutable resource, conflicts can occur.
IF MemMachine is configured with additional write scopes not listed here, overlap risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the repo read-only.
Do not grant shared write scopes.
Separate API credentials per agent.
Use locking for any shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add concurrency control around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can act on conversational context and external API inputs, so if it treats content from the writing-focused agent as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream travel-planning outputs. The repo agent does not verify facts or provide runtime checks, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF MemMachine uses text from the repo or copied prompts as authoritative guidance, incorrect advice can propagate.
IF downstream actions are taken from unverified generated content, the cascade becomes user-visible.
mitigations: Require source citations before acting on generated claims.
Insert a verification step between agents.
Limit MemMachine to suggestion-only mode.
Flag uncited assertions for review.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking against trusted sources.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. The only concrete compliance-relevant fact is that MemMachine handles long-term user facts and conversational context, while the repo agent is docs-only and does not itself process regulated data, so the pairwise compliance risk is limited and mostly conditional.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is entered into MemMachine, its retention and residency policies become relevant.
IF the repo is used to store or paste regulated data, compliance obligations may attach to the operator workflow.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both tools.
Review MemMachine retention settings.
Keep the repo free of personal data.
Document data-handling boundaries.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated fields.
